name: strategi-canon
//engines: THIS FIELD DESCRIBES WHAT THE APP NEEDS TO BUILD AND RUN, NOT WHAT `npm test` NEEDS, and
the difference is not academic: raising it to >=24.18.0 broke the Vercel deploy outright.
Vercel reads engines.node to choose the Node it builds with, and it can only satisfy a
range that overlaps a version it actually offers. >=20.18.1 resolves to the newest Node
Vercel has. >=24.18.0 resolved to nothing, so the deploy died with `Found invalid Node.js
Version` before it compiled a single file. The Next app itself never needed 24: it built
clean on the old floor and still does.
THE TEST REQUIREMENT IS REAL AND IT LIVES IN `pretest` INSTEAD. `npm test` runs TypeScript
through `node --test` with no build step and no loader flag, so it relies on node stripping
the types itself, which became unflagged only in 23.6. On an older node the suite does not
fail an assertion, it fails to PARSE, which reads as a broken repository rather than as an
unmet requirement. That was worth fixing and still is. It just cannot be fixed here, because
engines gates every consumer of this package including the one that only ever runs `next
build`. pretest gates exactly the script that has the requirement, and says so in words.
24.18.0 remains the number that matters for tests: it is NODE_VERSION in
canon_app/fetch_runtimes.py, the runtime bundled into the shipped package, and it is what
.github/workflows/tests.yml pins. pretest, fetch_runtimes.py and tests.yml agree. This
field deliberately does not, and a future edit that aligns it will break the deploy again.
//scripts: THE TEST GLOB IS QUOTED ON PURPOSE AND THE QUOTES ARE THE PORTABLE PART. Unquoted,
tests/*.test.ts is expanded by the SHELL, which works under sh on macOS and Linux and does
not work at all under the cmd.exe that npm uses on Windows, where the pattern would reach
node as a literal filename and the run would die on a file that does not exist. Quoted, the
shell passes the pattern through untouched and node's own test runner expands it, which it
does identically on all three platforms.
THE DIRECTORY FORM IS NOT AN OPTION HERE, which is worth recording because it is the obvious
thing to reach for. node --test tests/ picks up tests/gate-extract.ts, a helper that defines
no tests, and the run fails outright rather than skipping it. Matching *.test.ts is what
keeps helpers and tests in one directory without the helpers being treated as suites.
WHY THESE TWO SCRIPTS EXIST AT ALL. Before them there was no test script in this file and no
test step in CI, so the suites ran only when a person remembered the exact node incantation.
A mechanism nobody runs is the same as no mechanism, which is precisely the lesson the state
machine defect these suites guard had already taught twice.

scripts.pretest:
node -e "const need=[23,6,0],got=process.versions.node.split('.').map(Number);for(let i=0;i<3;i++){if(got[i]>need[i])process.exit(0);if(got[i]<need[i]){console.error('
  npm test needs Node >= 23.6.0 and this is Node '+process.versions.node+'.
  The suites are TypeScript run straight through node --test, so an older
  node cannot strip the types and every file dies on a PARSE error that
  looks like a broken repo. Install Node 24.18.0, the version CI pins and
  the version canon_app/fetch_runtimes.py bundles, then rerun npm test.
  Note engines.node stays at 20.18.1 on purpose: the app builds there and
  Vercel cannot deploy a range it has no version for.
');process.exit(1)}}"
